definition_zh: 次要的；中学的；第二位的；继发的
definition_en: less important than something else, relating to secondary school, coming second in order, or resulting from something else
core_image: 主干道旁的分岔小路，路口立着一块不起眼的小牌子
scene: 主路堵得水泄不通，他拐进一条次要的小路。He took a secondary road to avoid the traffic.
sceneCN: 这里 secondary 是「次要的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他走一条次要道路以避开拥堵。

senses.title: Less important
senses.definition: less important than the main thing
senses.definitionCN: 不如主要事物重要
senses.example: Safety is never a secondary concern.
senses.exampleCN: 安全从来都不是次要问题。
senses.why: This is the broad everyday sense of lower priority.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示优先级较低的宽泛日常义。

senses.title: Of secondary school
senses.definition: relating to education for older children
senses.definitionCN: 与较大儿童的教育有关
senses.example: She teaches at a secondary school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所中学教书。
senses.why: The school level comes after primary education.
senses.whyCN: 中学阶段在小学教育之后。

senses.title: Coming second
senses.definition: second in order, rank, or level
senses.definitionCN: 在顺序、等级或层次上居第二
senses.example: The report relied on secondary sources.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告依赖二手资料。
senses.why: A second-hand source is one step from the original.
senses.whyCN: 二手资料与原初来源隔了一步。

senses.title: Resulting from something
senses.definition: caused by or developing from an earlier condition
senses.definitionCN: 由先前状况引起或由此发展而来
senses.example: The doctor treated a secondary infection.
senses.exampleCN: 医生治疗了继发感染。
senses.why: Medical use names a condition that follows another.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法指紧随另一状况出现的病症。

intro.en: Secondary comes from Latin secundarius, from secundus, following or second.
intro.cn: secondary 源自拉丁语 secundarius，出自 secundus（跟随的、第二的）。

items.en: Secundus meant following or second.
items.cn: secundus 意为跟随的或第二的。

items.en: Secundarius meant of the second rank.
items.cn: secundarius 意为第二等级的。

items.en: Secondary entered English as a word for second rank.
items.cn: secondary 以「第二等级」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word described subordinate things and school levels.
items.cn: 该词用来形容从属事物与学校阶段。

items.en: Medicine added the sense of a following condition.
items.cn: 医学又增加了「继发状况」的义项。

note.en: Secondary is compared with similar-looking words and with words for lesser importance.
note.cn: 把 secondary 与形近词以及表示较次要的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Secondary means second in importance, level, or origin.
normalIntro.cn: secondary 意为在重要性、层级或来源上居第二。

normal.en: Secondary school follows primary school.
normal.cn: secondary school 是小学之后的中学。

normal.en: A secondary source is not the original.
normal.cn: secondary source 不是原始资料。

normal.en: Secondary means less important, not useless.
normal.cn: secondary 表示较次要，而非毫无用处。

normal.en: A secondary infection follows the first one.
normal.cn: secondary infection 是继发于初次感染的。

normal.en: Secondary shares its root with second.
normal.cn: secondary 与 second 同根。

abstract.en: Calling something secondary is a way of ranking the world.
abstract.cn: 称某事为次要，是在给世界排位。

abstract.en: What is secondary can still decide the outcome.
abstract.cn: 次要因素有时仍能决定结果。

abstract.en: Every first needs a second to follow it.
abstract.cn: 每一个第一都需要一个跟随的第二。

examples.en: Safety is never a secondary concern.
examples.cn: 安全从来都不是次要问题。

examples.en: She teaches at a secondary school.
The report relied on secondary sources.
examples.cn: 这份报告依赖二手资料。

dict_mnemonic.text: secondary 由 second（第二）加形容词后缀 -ary 构成，表示「排在第二位的、次要的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 secundarius（第二等级的），出自 secundus（第二），核心义「居其次的」。

sensesIntro.en: Secondary means less important, relating to secondary school, second in rank, or following another condition.
sensesIntro.cn: secondary 意为次要的、中学的、第二位的，或继发的。

core.en: Something that follows and ranks below a first.
core.cn: 跟随在第一之后、等级较低的事物。

branches.en: A matter of lower priority.
branches.cn: 优先级较低的事项。

branches.en: The school level after primary.
branches.cn: 小学之后的学校阶段。

branches.en: A rank or source one step from the first.
branches.cn: 距第一等一步之遥的等级或来源。

branches.en: A condition that follows another.
branches.cn: 紧随另一状况出现的病症。

branches.en: Lower importance and second rank often mean the same.
branches.cn: 较低重要性与第二等级常常是同一回事。

intro.en: Secondary builds on second, with words for order and priority.
intro.cn: secondary 以 second 为基础，构成表示顺序与优先级的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin secundus and secundarius are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 secundus 与 secundarius 是历史词根。

items.example: He finished second in the race.
items.exampleCN: 他在比赛中获得第二名。

items.meaning: second helpings or units of time
items.example: The clock ticked away the seconds.

items.exampleCN: 其次，我们需要更多时间。

items.example: The fund is used primarily, not secondarily.
items.exampleCN: 这笔资金用于主要用途，而非次要用途。

items.example: The secondariness of the issue was clear.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题的次要性很清楚。

items.example: They settled for a second-best option.
The parcel went by second-class mail.

definition_zh: 秘密；秘诀；秘密的；保密的
definition_en: something kept hidden from others, a method that works very well, or kept from public knowledge
core_image: 抽屉最里层压着一封没有署名的信，封口已经被摩挲得发白
scene: 她压低声音，把这件事只告诉了最好的朋友。She kept the secret from everyone else.
sceneCN: 这里 secret 是「秘密」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她对其他所有人都保守这个秘密。

senses.title: Something hidden
senses.definition: a fact or piece of information kept from others
senses.definitionCN: 对他人隐瞒的事实或信息
senses.example: She told me a secret.
senses.exampleCN: 她告诉了我一个秘密。
senses.why: This is the central everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最核心的日常义。

senses.title: A working method
senses.definition: a method or trick that produces a good result
senses.definitionCN: 能带来好结果的方法或窍门
senses.example: The recipe is a family secret.
senses.exampleCN: 这个配方是家族秘诀。
senses.why: A good method is often kept hidden like information.
senses.whyCN: 好方法常像信息一样被隐藏起来。

senses.title: Kept from others
senses.definition: known by only a few people or kept hidden
senses.definitionCN: 只有少数人知道或被隐藏的
senses.example: They held a secret meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他们举行了一次秘密会议。
senses.why: The noun sense becomes an adjective of concealment.
senses.whyCN: 名词义转化为表示隐藏的形容词。

intro.en: Secret comes from Latin secretus, set apart or hidden, from secernere, to separate.
intro.cn: secret 源自拉丁语 secretus（分开的、隐藏的），出自 secernere（分离）。

items.en: Secernere meant to separate or set apart.
items.cn: secernere 意为分开或隔离。

items.en: Secretus meant hidden or withdrawn.
items.cn: secretus 意为隐藏的或退避的。

items.en: Secret named something kept from view.
items.cn: secret 表示被藏起来的事物。

items.en: Secret entered English as both noun and adjective.
items.cn: secret 作为名词和形容词进入英语。

items.en: The word also names a special working method.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词也指特别的方法。

note.en: Secret is compared with similar-looking words and with words for hidden things.
note.cn: 把 secret 与形近词以及表示隐藏之物的词作比较。

entries.definition: the state of being kept hidden

normalIntro.en: A secret is hidden information, a hidden method, or the quality of being hidden.
normalIntro.cn: secret 是被隐藏的信息、隐藏的方法，或被隐藏的状态。

normal.en: Keep a secret means not telling others.
normal.cn: keep a secret 意为不告诉别人。

normal.en: In secret means quietly and privately.
normal.cn: in secret 意为悄悄地、私下地。

normal.en: Top secret is the highest level of secrecy.
normal.cn: top secret 是最高保密级别。

normal.en: The secret of success is a hidden working method.
normal.cn: the secret of success 指隐藏的成功方法。

normal.en: Secret and secretary share the same Latin root.
normal.cn: secret 与 secretary 共享拉丁词根。

abstract.en: A secret is something set apart from public view.
abstract.cn: 秘密是被从公众视野中分隔出来的事物。

abstract.en: Keeping a secret is a kind of power and a kind of burden.
abstract.cn: 保守秘密既是一种权力，也是一种负担。

abstract.en: A method becomes a secret when it is not shared.
abstract.cn: 方法不被分享时就成了秘诀。

examples.en: She told me a secret.
The recipe is a family secret.
They held a secret meeting.
examples.cn: 他们举行了一次秘密会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: secret 源自拉丁语 secretus（被分开、被藏起），词根 secernere 意为「分离」，核心是「与外界隔开」。

root: 源自拉丁语 secretus（隐藏的），出自 secernere（分离），核心义「与外界隔开、不公开」。

sensesIntro.en: Secret means hidden information, a special method, or something kept from public view.
sensesIntro.cn: secret 意为秘密信息、特别方法，或不让公众知道的事物。

core.en: Something separated from common knowledge.
core.cn: 被隔离在普通认知之外的事物。

branches.en: A fact kept from others.
branches.cn: 对他人隐瞒的事实。

branches.en: A hidden method that brings success.
branches.cn: 带来成功的隐藏方法。

branches.en: The quality of being kept hidden.
branches.cn: 被隐藏的状态。

branches.en: A secret fact and a secret meeting share the same concealment.
branches.cn: 秘密事实与秘密会议共享同一种隐藏。

branches.en: Information and technique can both be guarded.
branches.cn: 信息与技术都可能被严守。

intro.en: Secret forms words for hiding, privacy, and a tendency to conceal.
intro.cn: secret 构成表示隐藏、保密与爱遮掩的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin secretus and secernere are the historical sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 secretus 与 secernere 是历史来源。

items.example: The secret is safe with me.
items.exampleCN: 这个秘密在我这里很安全。
日记本里藏着她的秘密。

items.example: The plan was wrapped in secrecy.
He was secretive about his plans.
items.exampleCN: 他对自己的计划守口如瓶。
他的遮遮掩掩让朋友们担心。

items.meaning: to produce and release a substance
a substance released by a body

definition_en: a person who handles letters and records for an organization, an official of a club, or a government minister
core_image: 办公桌一角摞着待签的文件，电话听筒还夹在肩头
scene: 她把会议记录整理好，放到经理桌上。The secretary typed the minutes of the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 secretary 是「秘书」（第 1 个义项）；句意：秘书打出了会议记录。

senses.title: An office assistant
senses.definition: a person employed to handle letters, records, and office tasks
senses.definitionCN: 受雇处理信件、记录与办公事务的人
senses.example: The secretary answered the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 秘书接了电话。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的现代义。

senses.title: An organization officer
senses.definition: an official who keeps records for a club or organization
senses.definitionCN: 为俱乐部或组织保存记录的负责人
senses.example: She was elected secretary of the club.
senses.exampleCN: 她被选为俱乐部书记。
senses.why: Clubs use the title for their record keeper.
senses.whyCN: 俱乐部用该头衔称呼记录负责人。

senses.title: A government minister
senses.definition: a senior government official in charge of a department
senses.definitionCN: 负责某个部门的高级政府官员
senses.example: The Foreign Secretary gave a speech.
senses.exampleCN: 外交大臣发表了讲话。
senses.why: In some governments the title names a minister.
senses.whyCN: 在某些政府中该头衔指部长。

intro.en: Secretary comes from Latin secretarius, an officer trusted with secrets.
intro.cn: secretary 源自拉丁语 secretarius，指受托掌管机密的人员。

items.en: Secretum meant a secret.
items.cn: secretum 意为秘密。

items.en: Secretarius meant a confidential officer.
items.cn: secretarius 意为掌管机密的人员。

items.en: Secretary entered English for a trusted clerk.
items.cn: secretary 以「受信任的文书」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word spread to clubs and government offices.
items.cn: 该词扩展到俱乐部与政府机构。

items.en: Some countries use it as the title of a minister.
items.cn: 一些国家用该词作为部长头衔。

note.en: Secretary is compared with similar-looking words and with words for assistants and officials.
note.cn: 把 secretary 与形近词以及表示助理、官员的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who keeps records or serves customers

normalIntro.en: A secretary keeps records and handles office work, and the title also names club officers and ministers.
normalIntro.cn: secretary 负责记录与办公事务，也可指俱乐部干事与部长。

normal.en: Secretary contains secret, because the job once involved trust.
normal.cn: secretary 含有 secret，因为这个职务曾与信任机密有关。

normal.en: The plural is secretaries, changing y to ies.
normal.cn: 复数是 secretaries，把 y 变成 ies。

normal.en: A secretary general leads an international organization.
normal.cn: secretary general 领导一个国际组织。

normal.en: A press secretary speaks for a government.
normal.cn: press secretary 为政府发声。

normal.en: Secretarial work includes typing and filing.
normal.cn: secretarial work 包括打字与归档。

abstract.en: The keeper of records holds the memory of an office.
abstract.cn: 记录保管者掌握着一个机构的内存。

abstract.en: Trust is the oldest part of the job.
abstract.cn: 信任是这份工作最古老的部分。

abstract.en: A small title can grow into a government post.
abstract.cn: 一个小头衔也能成长为政府要职。

examples.en: The secretary answered the phone.
She was elected secretary of the club.
The Foreign Secretary gave a speech.

dict_mnemonic.text: secretary 源自拉丁语 secretarius（掌管机密者），由 secret（秘密）加表示职位的后缀构成。

root: 源自拉丁语 secretarius（机密掌管者），出自 secretum（秘密），核心义「受托处理事务与记录的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Secretary means an office assistant, a club officer who keeps records, or a government minister.
sensesIntro.cn: secretary 意为办公秘书、负责记录的俱乐部干事，或政府部长。

core.en: A trusted person who keeps records and handles affairs.
core.cn: 受托保管记录、处理事务的人。

branches.en: An assistant who runs an office.
branches.cn: 维持办公室运转的助理。

branches.en: An officer who keeps a group's records.
branches.cn: 为团体保存记录的干事。

branches.en: A minister in charge of a department.
branches.cn: 负责一个部门的部长。

branches.en: Office and club roles both center on records and trust.
branches.cn: 办公与俱乐部角色都以记录和信任为核心。

branches.en: The title rises from club officer to state office.
branches.cn: 这个头衔从俱乐部干事升至国家职务。

intro.en: Secretary forms words for the office, the body of staff, and the post itself.
intro.cn: secretary 构成表示秘书工作、秘书处与职位的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin secretarius and secretum are the historical sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 secretarius 与 secretum 是历史来源。

items.example: The two secretaries share an office.
items.exampleCN: 两位秘书共用一间办公室。

items.meaning: the staff or office of a secretary

items.example: He held the secretaryship for two years.
The secret stayed in the office.
The meeting was held in secrecy.
items.exampleCN: 会议在保密状态下举行。

items.example: The office was secretive about the plan.
items.exampleCN: 办公室对计划守口如瓶。

latinEntries.exampleCN: secretarius 意为掌管机密的官员。

definition_en: in a way that is intended to be hidden from others
core_image: 门缝里透出一线灯光，有人正把箱子悄悄推到床底下
scene: 他趁家人睡下，悄悄把礼物藏进衣柜。He secretly hid the gift in the wardrobe.
sceneCN: 这里 secretly 是「秘密地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他偷偷把礼物藏进衣柜。

senses.title: In a hidden way
senses.definition: in a manner kept hidden from other people
senses.definitionCN: 以对他人隐藏的方式
senses.example: They secretly planned a surprise party.
senses.exampleCN: 他们秘密策划了一场惊喜派对。
senses.why: This is the general adverb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是该副词的宽泛义。

senses.title: Without being noticed
senses.definition: doing something without other people noticing
senses.definitionCN: 在别人没有察觉的情况下做某事
senses.example: The letter was secretly copied.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信被偷偷复印了。
senses.why: The focus shifts from secrecy to avoiding notice.
senses.whyCN: 重点从保密转向避免被发现。

senses.title: Within one's heart
senses.definition: felt privately without being expressed
senses.definitionCN: 私下怀有而不表达出来
senses.example: He secretly hoped she would stay.
senses.exampleCN: 他暗自希望她会留下。
senses.why: Private feeling is another kind of hiddenness.
senses.whyCN: 私下的情感是另一种隐藏。

intro.en: Secretly is secret with the adverb suffix -ly, from Latin secretus.
intro.cn: secretly 是 secret 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，secret 源自拉丁语 secretus。

items.en: Secretus meant hidden or set apart.
items.cn: secretus 意为隐藏的或分开的。

items.en: Secret named something kept from view.
items.cn: secret 表示被藏起来的事物。

items.en: Secret entered English as noun and adjective.
items.cn: secret 作为名词和形容词进入英语。

items.en: The adverb secretly formed with -ly.
items.cn: 副词 secretly 由 -ly 构成。

items.en: Secretly now covers hidden action and private feeling.
items.cn: 现代英语中 secretly 涵盖隐秘行动与私下情感。

note.en: Secretly is compared with similar-looking words and with words for privacy.
note.cn: 把 secretly 与形近词以及表示私下、隐秘的词作比较。

entries.definition: in a hidden or secret way

normalIntro.en: Secretly means doing, keeping, or feeling something out of others' sight.
normalIntro.cn: secretly 意为在他人视线之外做、藏或感受某事。

normal.en: Secretly is secret plus -ly.
normal.cn: secretly 由 secret 加 -ly 构成。

normal.en: Secretly plan means plan without telling.
normal.cn: secretly plan 意为不告知地策划。

normal.en: Secretly hope is a private feeling.
normal.cn: secretly hope 是私下里的愿望。

normal.en: Secretly record raises questions of consent.
normal.cn: 偷偷录制会引发知情同意的问题。

normal.en: The word ends in -ly like most adverbs.
normal.cn: 这个词像大多数副词一样以 -ly 结尾。

abstract.en: Doing something secretly changes its meaning.
abstract.cn: 偷偷做某事会改变这件事的意义。

abstract.en: Private hope and hidden action share one adverb.
abstract.cn: 私下愿望与隐秘行动共用一个副词。

abstract.en: Not being seen is not the same as doing no harm.
abstract.cn: 不被看见并不等于没有造成伤害。

examples.en: They secretly planned a surprise party.
examples.cn: 他们秘密策划了一场惊喜派对。

examples.en: He secretly hoped she would stay.
The letter was secretly copied.

dict_mnemonic.text: secretly 由 secret（秘密的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，表示「以秘密的方式」。

root: 由 secret（秘密的）加后缀 -ly 构成；secret 源自拉丁语 secretus（隐藏的）。

sensesIntro.en: Secretly means in a hidden way, without being noticed, or in one's private heart.
sensesIntro.cn: secretly 意为秘密地、不被人察觉地，或内心暗暗地。

core.en: Acting or feeling outside the view of others.
core.cn: 在他人视野之外行动或感受。

branches.en: Doing something in a concealed way.
branches.cn: 以隐蔽方式做某事。

branches.en: Acting without others noticing.
branches.cn: 在别人未察觉时行动。

branches.en: Holding a feeling privately.
branches.cn: 私下怀有某种情感。

branches.en: Concealment and avoiding notice usually go together.
branches.cn: 隐藏与避免被注意通常同时发生。

branches.en: A hidden act and a hidden hope both stay out of sight.
branches.cn: 隐秘行动与隐秘愿望都留在视线之外。

intro.en: Secretly belongs to the secret family of hiddenness.
intro.cn: secretly 属于表示隐藏的 secret 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin secretus and secernere stand behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 secretus 与 secernere 是该词族的来源。

items.example: They kept the secret for years.
items.exampleCN: 他们多年保守这个秘密。
盒子里藏着旧日的秘密。

items.example: The deal was done in secrecy.
items.exampleCN: 这笔交易在秘密中完成。

items.example: The cells secrete a thin fluid.
items.exampleCN: 细胞分泌一种稀薄液体。

definition_en: one of the parts into which something is divided, a department, a part of a book, or a cut-away view
core_image: 厚书摊开在桌上，书签夹在标着章节号的那一页
scene: 他翻到讲方法的章节，用铅笔在页边画了个圈。She turned to the section on methods.
sceneCN: 这里 section 是「章节」（第 3 个义项）；句意：她翻到讲方法的那一节。

senses.title: One of the parts
senses.definition: one of the parts into which a whole is divided
senses.definitionCN: 整体被分成的部分之一
senses.example: This section of the road is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 这段路封闭了。
senses.why: This is the broad physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是宽泛的实物义。

senses.title: A department
senses.definition: a separate part of an organization or shop
senses.definitionCN: 组织或商店中独立的部门
senses.example: She works in the sports section.
senses.exampleCN: 她在体育部工作。
senses.why: Organizations divide work into sections.
senses.whyCN: 组织把工作分成各个部门。

senses.title: A part of a book
senses.definition: a part of a book, report, or newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 书、报告或报纸中的一个部分
senses.example: Read the first section of the report.
senses.exampleCN: 读报告的第一节。
senses.why: Written works are divided into sections.
senses.whyCN: 文字作品被分成章节。

senses.title: A cut-away view
senses.definition: a view of something as if cut through
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛被切开后看到的样子
senses.example: The diagram shows a cross section of the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 图里展示了管道的横截面。
senses.why: The original sense is literally a cutting.
senses.whyCN: 本义就是「切下来的部分」。

intro.en: Section comes from Latin sectio, a cutting, from secare, to cut.
intro.cn: section 源自拉丁语 sectio（切割），出自 secare（切）。

items.en: Secare meant to cut.
items.cn: secare 意为切。

items.en: Sectio meant a cutting or a piece cut off.
items.cn: sectio 意为切割或切下的部分。

items.en: Section entered English as a part cut from a whole.
items.cn: section 以「从整体切下的部分」进入英语。

items.en: Books and organizations began to use sections.
items.cn: 书籍与组织开始使用 section 划分。

items.en: The word also names a technical cross-section.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词也指技术性的横截面。

note.en: Section is compared with similar-looking words and with words for parts.
note.cn: 把 section 与形近词以及表示部分的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A section is a part cut from a whole, whether a road, a shop, a book, or a pipe.

normal.en: Section and sector both come from a root meaning to cut.

normal.en: A newspaper has a sports section and a business section.
normal.cn: 报纸有体育版和商业版。

normal.en: Read the report section by section.
normal.cn: 要一部分一部分地读报告。

normal.en: A cross section shows the inside of an object.
normal.cn: 横截面展示物体内部。

normal.en: A subsection is a smaller section inside one.
normal.cn: subsection 是章节内更小的节。

abstract.en: To understand a whole, we cut it into sections.
abstract.cn: 为了理解整体，我们把它切成部分。

abstract.en: Every section belongs to something larger.
abstract.cn: 每个部分都属于某个更大的整体。

abstract.en: A cross section reveals what the surface hides.
abstract.cn: 横截面揭示表面所隐藏的东西。

examples.en: This section of the road is closed.
She works in the sports section.
Read the first section of the report.

definition_en: a distinct part of an economy or society, a particular area of business, a slice-shaped part of a circle, or a separate district
core_image: 一张饼图被切成几块，每块颜色不同，旁边标着各自的比例
scene: 报告用一张饼图拆开了国民经济的几大部门。The service sector now employs most workers.

senses.title: Part of an economy
senses.definition: a distinct part of a country's economy or society
senses.definitionCN: 一国经济或社会中相对独立的一部分
senses.example: The service sector is growing fast.
senses.exampleCN: 服务业部门增长很快。
senses.why: Economists divide national activity into sectors.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把国民活动划分成若干部门。

senses.title: Area of business
senses.definition: a particular area of business activity
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定的商业活动领域
senses.example: She works in the technology sector.
senses.exampleCN: 她在科技行业工作。
senses.why: The word labels industries such as banking or farming.
senses.whyCN: 该词用来标记银行、农业等行业。

senses.title: Slice of a circle
senses.definition: a plane figure bounded by two radii and an arc
senses.definitionCN: 由两条半径和一段弧围成的平面图形
senses.example: Draw a sector of the circle in the diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 在图上画一个圆的扇形。
senses.why: The geometric sense keeps the idea of a cut-out part.
senses.whyCN: 几何义保留了「切分出来的一块」这个意象。

senses.title: Separate district
senses.definition: a distinct part of an area, especially in military use
senses.definitionCN: 某一区域中相对独立的部分，尤用于军事
senses.example: Troops held the northern sector of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 部队控制了城市的北部区域。
senses.why: A sector can also be a piece of physical ground.
senses.whyCN: sector 也可以指地面上划分出的一块。

items.en: It extended to parts of an economy.
items.cn: 它又扩展到经济部门的含义。

items.en: Today it labels industries and city districts.
items.cn: 如今它用来标记各行业与城区。

normalIntro.en: Sector means a cut-out part of a larger whole.
normalIntro.cn: sector 意为从更大整体中切分出来的一块。

normal.en: Sector comes from a Latin verb meaning to cut.
normal.cn: sector 出自一个意为「切」的拉丁语动词。

normal.en: Each slice of a pie chart is a sector.
normal.cn: 饼图中的每一块都是扇形。

normal.en: The service sector sells services, not goods.
normal.cn: 服务业部门卖的是服务而非货物。

normal.en: The public sector is run by the government.

normal.en: Sector and section share the same root.

abstract.en: To divide the world into sectors is a way of seeing it.
abstract.cn: 把世界分成部门，是一种观察世界的方式。

abstract.en: From inside, a sector can look like the whole.

abstract.en: A sector is always a part of a larger circle.

examples.en: The service sector is growing fast.

definition_zh: 安全的；牢固的；获得；使安全
definition_en: safe from danger, firmly fixed, to succeed in getting something, or to make something safe
core_image: 门上新换的锁舌咔哒一声扣进锁扣，链条也挂好了
scene: 他换了新锁，又把窗户逐一检查了一遍。She secured the door before leaving.
sceneCN: 这里 secure 是「使安全」（第 4 个义项）；句意：她离开前把门锁好。

senses.title: Safe from danger
senses.definition: protected from harm or risk
senses.definitionCN: 受到保护而免于伤害或风险
senses.example: Keep your passport in a secure place.
senses.exampleCN: 把护照放在安全的地方。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of being free from danger.
senses.whyCN: 这是「免于危险」的基本义。

senses.title: Firmly fixed
senses.definition: fixed so firmly that it cannot move or be opened
senses.definitionCN: 固定得很牢，不会移动或被打开
senses.example: Make sure the ladder is secure.
senses.exampleCN: 确保梯子固定牢靠。
senses.why: Something firmly fastened is also safe.
senses.whyCN: 固定牢靠的东西同样是安全的。

senses.title: Obtain
senses.definition: to succeed in getting something
senses.definitionCN: 成功地得到某物
senses.example: She secured a place at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她获得了大学的录取名额。
senses.why: Getting something safely is the verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 稳妥地得到某物，是它的动词义。

senses.title: Make safe
senses.definition: to protect something from danger or loss
senses.definitionCN: 保护某物免受危险或损失
senses.example: Guards secured the building.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫守住了大楼。
senses.why: The verb can mean to fasten or guard a place.
senses.whyCN: 动词也可表示把某处锁好或守住。

intro.en: Secure comes from Latin securus, free from care, from se- without and cura care.
intro.cn: secure 源自拉丁语 securus（无忧的），由 se-（无）与 cura（忧虑）构成。

items.en: Cura meant care or worry.
items.cn: cura 意为关心、忧虑。

items.en: Securus described a person free from care.
items.cn: securus 形容一个人无忧无虑。

items.en: Securitas named safety and freedom from fear.
items.cn: securitas 指安全与免于恐惧。

items.en: English secure first meant free from fear.
items.cn: 英语 secure 最初意为免于恐惧。

items.en: The word later meant to fasten and to obtain.
items.cn: 后来该词又表示固定牢靠与获得。

note.en: Secure is compared with similar-looking words and with words for safety.
note.cn: 把 secure 与形近词以及表示安全的词作比较。

entries.definition: in a safe or firm way

normalIntro.en: Secure means free from care, firmly fixed, or safely obtained.
normalIntro.cn: secure 意为无忧、牢固或稳妥地获得。

normal.en: The prefix se- means without.
normal.cn: 前缀 se- 意为「无」。

normal.en: Cura means care, so secure means without care.
normal.cn: cura 意为忧虑，所以 secure 就是无忧。

normal.en: A secure door is firmly locked.
normal.cn: secure 的门是锁得牢靠的。

normal.en: You can secure a ticket before they sell out.
normal.cn: 你可以在售罄前把票拿到手。

normal.en: Security is the noun from secure.
normal.cn: security 是 secure 的名词形式。

abstract.en: To secure something is to take worry out of it.
abstract.cn: 把某物 secured，就是把忧虑从中拿掉。

abstract.en: Safety is often a matter of firm fastening.
abstract.cn: 安全往往就取决于是否固定牢靠。

abstract.en: What is securely held can still be lost if no one watches.
abstract.cn: 即便牢牢在握，无人看管也可能失去。

examples.en: Keep your passport in a secure place.
examples.cn: 把护照放在安全的地方。

examples.en: Make sure the ladder is secure.
She secured a place at university.
examples.cn: 她获得了大学的录取名额。

branches.en: A person or place free from danger.

branches.en: Something obtained with certainty.
branches.cn: 稳妥得到的东西。

branches.en: An act of guarding or locking.
branches.cn: 守住或锁好的动作。

items.example: The room is secure at night.

items.exampleCN: 安全是我们首要的关切。

items.meaning: in a safe or firm way

items.example: He felt insecure in the new job.
items.exampleCN: 他在新工作中感到不安。

items.meaning: a feeling of not being safe
items.example: She hid her insecurity with jokes.
items.exampleCN: 她用玩笑掩饰自己的不安全感。

items.meaning: a paid job with little work
items.example: He treated the post as a sinecure.
items.exampleCN: 他把这个职位当成闲职。

definition_en: the state of being safe, protection against danger, the guards who protect a place, or financial assets such as shares
core_image: 安检口的传送带缓缓转动，行李一件接一件滑进扫描机
scene: 进大楼前，每个人都要把包放上检查台。Airport security checked every bag.
sceneCN: 这里 security 是「保安」（第 3 个义项）；句意：机场保安检查了每一个包。

senses.title: State of safety
senses.definition: the state of being free from danger
senses.definitionCN: 免于危险的状态
senses.example: The security of the passengers came first.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客的安全是第一位的。
senses.why: This is the broad noun sense of being safe.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示「处于安全中」的宽泛名词义。

senses.title: Protection
senses.definition: things done to protect someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 为保护人或物而采取的措施
senses.example: The bank added extra security after the robbery.
senses.exampleCN: 抢劫案之后银行加强了安保措施。
senses.why: Concrete measures turn safety into a countable idea.
senses.whyCN: 具体措施把「安全」变成了可计数的概念。

senses.title: Guards
senses.definition: the people whose job is to protect a place
senses.definitionCN: 以保护某处为职责的人员
senses.example: Security stopped him at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 保安在大门口拦住了他。
senses.why: The people who guard a building are called security.
senses.whyCN: 看守大楼的人被统称为保安。

senses.title: Financial assets
senses.definition: shares, bonds, and other financial investments
senses.definitionCN: 股票、债券及其他金融投资品
senses.example: He invested in government securities.
senses.exampleCN: 他投资了政府证券。
senses.why: A financial sense grew from documents that secure a claim.
senses.whyCN: 证券义源于「能保障某种权益的凭证」。

branches.en: Safety is both a state and the work that keeps it.
branches.cn: 安全既是状态，也是维持它的工作。

intro.cn: security 与 cure 等词共享拉丁词根 cura（忧虑）。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 securitas 与 securus 是历史词根。

items.example: Security is tight at the airport.

definition_en: to notice something with your eyes, to understand, to meet someone, or to experience something
core_image: 山顶上，云海在脚下缓缓翻涌，远处透出一线天光
scene: 他站在山顶，看见云海从脚下漫过来。From the top he could see the clouds rolling in below.
sceneCN: 这里 see 是「看见」（第 1 个义项）；句意：从山顶他能看见云层在下方翻滚而来。

collocations.phrase: as far as I can see

senses.title: Perceive with eyes
senses.definition: to notice something with your eyes
senses.definitionCN: 用眼睛察觉到某物
senses.example: I saw a light in the window.
senses.exampleCN: 我看见窗户里有灯光。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense of sight.
senses.whyCN: 这是视觉的基本物理义。

senses.title: Understand
senses.definition: to understand something
senses.definitionCN: 理解某事
senses.example: I see what you mean.
senses.exampleCN: 我明白你的意思。
senses.why: Understanding is pictured as seeing a point.
senses.whyCN: 理解被比作「看见」某个要点。

senses.title: Meet someone
senses.definition: to meet or visit someone
senses.definitionCN: 与某人见面或拜访某人
senses.example: I will see the doctor tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 我明天去看医生。
senses.why: Meeting a person is expressed as seeing them.
senses.whyCN: 与人见面常用 see 来表达。

senses.title: Experience
senses.definition: to experience or witness an event
senses.definitionCN: 经历或目睹某个事件
senses.example: The city has seen many changes.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市经历了许多变化。
senses.why: Seeing an event means living through it.
senses.whyCN: 「看见」一个事件，也就是亲历它。

intro.en: See comes from Old English seon, a Germanic verb with strong past forms saw and seen.
intro.cn: see 源自古英语 seon，是日耳曼语动词，过去式为 saw、过去分词为 seen。

items.en: Seon meant to see with the eyes.
items.cn: seon 意为用眼睛看见。

items.en: Sihth, the noun for sight, grew beside it.
items.cn: 表示视力的名词 sihth 与它并行发展。

items.en: The verb kept its strong past forms saw and seen.
items.cn: 该动词保留了强变化过去式 saw 与 seen。

items.en: See added the sense of understanding a point.
items.cn: see 增加了「明白要点」的义项。

items.en: It also came to mean meet and experience.
items.cn: 它又用来表示会见与经历。

note.en: See is compared with similar-looking words and with other verbs of looking.
note.cn: 把 see 与形近词以及其他表示「看」的动词作比较。

the part of a plant that can grow

normalIntro.en: See is the everyday verb for sight, understanding, meeting, and experience.
normalIntro.cn: see 是表示看见、明白、会见与经历的日常动词。

normal.en: The past tense of see is saw, not seed.
normal.cn: see 的过去式是 saw，不是 seed。

normal.en: I see means I understand.
normal.cn: I see 的意思是「我明白了」。

normal.en: You see a doctor when you are ill.
normal.cn: 生病时你去看医生。

normal.en: A city can see many changes over time.
normal.cn: 一座城市会经历许多变化。

normal.en: See, look, and watch differ in how long you attend.
normal.cn: see、look、watch 在注视时长上不同。

abstract.en: To see is to let the world enter you.
abstract.cn: 看见，就是让世界进入你。

abstract.en: Understanding is sight turned inward.
abstract.cn: 理解是转向内心的视力。

abstract.en: What we have seen shapes what we expect to see.
abstract.cn: 我们见过的东西，塑造了我们期待看见的东西。

examples.en: I saw a light in the window.
I see what you mean.
The city has seen many changes.
examples.cn: 这座城市经历了许多变化。

core.en: To take something in through the eyes, and then through the mind.
core.cn: 先用眼睛、再用心智去接收某物。

branches.en: Light reaches the eyes.
branches.cn: 光线进入眼睛。

branches.en: A point becomes clear in the mind.
branches.cn: 某个要点在心中变得清楚。

branches.en: One person comes before another.
branches.cn: 一个人出现在另一个人面前。

branches.en: An event is lived through.
branches.cn: 一个事件被亲历。

branches.en: Seeing and understanding share one verb.
branches.cn: 看见与明白共用一个动词。

intro.cn: see 是日耳曼语本族动词，并由 sight 构成若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: This is a Germanic word, so there are no Latin base forms to add.

items.example: No one could foresee the result.

items.meaning: a person who claims to see the future

definition_zh: 种子；起因；播种；种子选手
definition_en: the small part of a plant from which a new plant grows, the origin of a feeling or situation, to plant seeds, or a ranked player in a tournament
core_image: 掌心摊开几粒小小的褐色种子，外壳上还沾着泥土
scene: 春天一到，他把种子埋进松软的土里。They planted the seed in early spring.
sceneCN: 这里 seed 是「种子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们在早春播下种子。

senses.title: Plant seed
senses.definition: the small hard part of a plant that can grow into a new plant
senses.definitionCN: 植物中能长出新生植株的坚硬小部分
senses.example: She planted seeds in small pots.
senses.exampleCN: 她把种子种在小花盆里。
senses.why: This is the everyday botanical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的植物学义。

senses.title: Origin
senses.definition: the beginning or cause of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事的开端或起因
senses.example: The remark planted the seed of doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 那句话种下了怀疑的种子。
senses.why: An idea that will grow is pictured as a seed.
senses.whyCN: 将要生长起来的想法被比作种子。

senses.title: Plant seeds
senses.definition: to plant seeds in the ground
senses.definitionCN: 把种子播进土里
senses.example: Farmers seed the fields in April.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在四月给田地播种。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb for sowing.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示播种的动词。

senses.title: Ranked player
senses.definition: a player ranked so as not to meet other top players early
senses.definitionCN: 被排定名次、以免过早与其他高手相遇的选手
senses.example: He is the top seed in the tournament.
senses.exampleCN: 他是本次比赛的头号种子。
senses.why: Tournaments seed players like plants in ordered rows.
senses.whyCN: 赛事像分行播种一样给选手排位。

intro.en: Seed comes from Old English sæd, from a Germanic root for sowing.
intro.cn: seed 源自古英语 sæd，出自日耳曼语中表示播种的词根。

items.en: Sæd meant that which is sown.
items.cn: sæd 意为被播下的东西。

items.en: The word also covered offspring and origin.
items.cn: 该词也涵盖后代与起源。

items.en: Seed kept both the plant and the origin senses.
items.cn: seed 同时保留植物与起源两种含义。

items.en: The verb grew from the noun.
items.cn: 动词义由名词义发展而来。

items.en: Sport gave the word its ranked-player sense.
items.cn: 体育又赋予它「种子选手」的义项。

note.en: Seed is compared with similar-looking words and with words for grains and origins.
note.cn: 把 seed 与形近词以及表示谷粒、起源的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small hard seed of a cereal plant
the inner part of a seed or nut
a young plant grown from a seed

normalIntro.en: Seed means the start of a plant and, by extension, the start of anything.
normalIntro.cn: seed 指植物的起点，也引申为任何事物的开端。

normal.en: A seed holds a whole plant in miniature.
normal.cn: 一粒种子里缩小地藏着一整株植物。

normal.en: The seed of doubt is a very small beginning.
normal.cn: 「怀疑的种子」是极小的开端。

normal.en: Farmers seed their fields in spring.
normal.cn: 农民在春天给田地播种。

normal.en: The top seed is the player ranked first.
normal.cn: 头号种子是排名第一的选手。

normal.en: Seed and sow are old farming words.
normal.cn: seed 与 sow 都是古老的农事词。

abstract.en: Every large thing begins as a seed of something small.
abstract.cn: 每件大事都始于某个微小事物的种子。

abstract.en: A seed waits before it grows.
abstract.cn: 种子在生长之前会等待。

abstract.en: What you seed today shapes the harvest later.
abstract.cn: 今天播下的种子，决定以后的收成。

examples.en: She planted seeds in small pots.
examples.cn: 她把种子种在小花盆里。

examples.en: The remark planted the seed of doubt.
examples.cn: 那句话种下了怀疑的种子。

examples.en: He is the top seed in the tournament.
examples.cn: 他是本次比赛的头号种子。

dict_mnemonic.text: seed 是日耳曼语本族词，本义「被播下之物」，由植物种子引申为起因、播种与种子选手。

core.en: A small beginning that holds a larger growth.
core.cn: 蕴藏着更大生长的小小开端。

branches.en: The hard part that becomes a plant.
branches.cn: 能长成植株的坚硬部分。

branches.en: The small start of a feeling or event.
branches.cn: 情绪或事件的小小起点。

branches.en: The act of putting seeds in soil.
branches.cn: 把种子放进土里的动作。

branches.en: A player placed in order like a sown row.
branches.cn: 像播种成行一样排出名次的选手。

branches.en: Plant and origin share the image of growth.

definition_en: to try to find something, to ask for help or advice, or to try to achieve something
core_image: 手电光在堆满纸箱的仓库里来回扫，脚下扬起细尘
scene: 他在仓库里一排排地找那只丢失的箱子。He sought the missing box among the shelves.
sceneCN: 这里 seek 是「寻找」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他在货架间寻找那只丢失的箱子。

senses.title: Try to find
senses.definition: to try to find someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 试图找到某人或某物
senses.example: She sought the missing keys everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 她到处寻找丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of searching for something.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示搜寻某物的基本义。

senses.title: Ask for
senses.definition: to ask for something such as help or advice
senses.definitionCN: 请求帮助、建议等
senses.example: He sought advice from his teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他向老师寻求建议。
senses.why: People seek what they need from others.
senses.whyCN: 人们向他人寻求自己需要的东西。

senses.title: Try to achieve
senses.definition: to try to do or achieve something
senses.definitionCN: 试图做或达成某事
senses.example: The company seeks to cut costs.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司试图削减成本。
senses.why: Seek plus to marks an aim being pursued.
senses.whyCN: seek 后接 to，表示正在追求的目标。

intro.en: Seek comes from Old English secan, a strong verb whose past tense is sought.
intro.cn: seek 源自古英语 secan，是强变化动词，过去式为 sought。

items.en: Secan meant to look for or strive after.
items.cn: secan 意为寻找或追求。

items.en: The past form sohte later became sought.
items.cn: 其过去式 sohte 后来演变为 sought。

items.en: The verb kept both the search and request senses.
items.cn: 该动词同时保留寻找与请求两种含义。

items.en: Seek to became a common way to state a goal.
items.cn: seek to 成为陈述目标的常见说法。

items.en: The word appears in law, business, and everyday speech.
items.cn: 该词出现在法律、商务与日常表达中。

note.en: Seek is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs of searching.
note.cn: 把 seek 与形近词以及表示搜寻的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Seek means to look for, ask for, or try to achieve.
normalIntro.cn: seek 意为寻找、寻求或试图达成。

normal.en: The past tense of seek is sought.
normal.cn: seek 的过去式是 sought。

normal.en: You seek help when you cannot manage alone.
normal.cn: 独自应付不了时，你就寻求帮助。

normal.en: Seek advice before making a big decision.
normal.cn: 做重大决定前先征求意见。

normal.en: Seek to do something means try to do it.
normal.cn: seek to do something 意为试图去做。

normal.en: A job seeker is looking for work.
normal.cn: 求职者正在找工作。

abstract.en: To seek is to admit something is missing.
abstract.cn: 去寻找，就是承认有所缺失。

abstract.en: What we seek shapes where we look.
abstract.cn: 我们寻找什么，决定了我们看向何处。

abstract.en: Some things are found only after long seeking.
abstract.cn: 有些东西要寻很久才能找到。

examples.en: She sought the missing keys everywhere.
examples.cn: 她到处寻找丢失的钥匙。

examples.en: He sought advice from his teacher.
The company seeks to cut costs.
examples.cn: 这家公司试图削减成本。

core.en: To move toward something one does not yet have.
core.cn: 朝自己尚未拥有的事物靠近。

branches.en: Looking for a lost thing.
branches.cn: 寻找丢失的东西。

branches.en: Asking others for what you need.
branches.cn: 向他人请求自己需要的东西。

branches.en: Aiming at a goal over time.
branches.cn: 长期朝着目标努力。

branches.en: Searching and striving both look forward.
branches.cn: 寻找与追求都朝向未来。

branches.en: A request is a search for help.
branches.cn: 请求其实就是寻求帮助。

intro.en: Seek forms a small family of compounds and one common irregular past form.
intro.cn: seek 构成少量复合词，并有一个常见的不规则过去式。

items.example: We seek a quiet place to rest.
items.exampleCN: 我们寻找一个安静的地方休息。

items.example: They sought shelter from the rain.
He is seeking a new challenge.

items.meaning: a person who looks for something
items.exampleCN: 寻求者们在黎明前就到了。
求职者在办公室外排队。
他活像个追求享乐的人。

definition_en: to appear to be something or to appear to do something, or to make a statement less direct
core_image: 雾里一个模糊的人影，轮廓忽近忽远
scene: 雾里那个人影晃了一下，看着像熟人。The figure seemed familiar in the fog.
sceneCN: 这里 seem 是「看起来像」（第 1 个义项）；句意：雾中的身影看起来很熟悉。

senses.title: Appear to be
senses.definition: to give the impression of being something
senses.definitionCN: 给人某种印象，好像是某物
senses.example: The house seems very old.
senses.exampleCN: 这房子看起来很旧。
senses.why: This is the common linking use before an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这是接形容词时最常见的系动词用法。

senses.title: Appear to do
senses.definition: to give the impression of doing something
senses.definitionCN: 给人正在做某事的印象
senses.example: She seems to know the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她似乎知道答案。
senses.why: Seem can also introduce an action.
senses.whyCN: seem 也可以引出某个动作。

senses.title: Softening a statement
senses.definition: used to make a claim less direct or less certain
senses.definitionCN: 用于让陈述更委婉、更不确定
senses.example: It seems we have a problem.
senses.exampleCN: 看来我们遇到麻烦了。
senses.why: The word softens what follows it.
senses.whyCN: 该词使其后的说法变得委婉。

intro.en: Seem comes from Old Norse soema, to befit, from a root meaning fitting or suitable.

items.en: Soema meant to befit or suit.
items.cn: soema 意为适合、相称。

items.en: The related adjective meant fitting.
items.cn: 相关形容词意为合适的。

items.en: English seem first meant to be fitting.
items.cn: 英语 seem 最初意为合适。

items.en: It shifted toward appear to be.
items.cn: 它逐渐转向「看起来是」的意思。

items.en: It now also softens statements politely.
items.cn: 如今它也用来礼貌地缓和陈述。

note.en: Seem is compared with similar-looking words and with other linking verbs.
note.cn: 把 seem 与形近词以及其他系动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Seem means to look a certain way without proving it.

normal.en: Seem is a linking verb like appear.
normal.cn: seem 和 appear 一样是系动词。

normal.en: It seems that means it appears that.
normal.cn: it seems that 意为「看起来……」。

normal.en: She seems tired means she looks tired.
normal.cn: she seems tired 意为她看起来很累。

normal.en: Seem to do describes an apparent action.
normal.cn: seem to do 描述一个看似发生的动作。

normal.en: Seemly and unseemly come from the same root.
normal.cn: seemly 与 unseemly 同出一源。

abstract.en: Seem lives in the gap between appearance and fact.
abstract.cn: seem 存在于外表与事实的缝隙里。

abstract.en: What seems true may only be partly true.
abstract.cn: 看似为真的，也许只是部分为真。

abstract.en: Every judgment begins with how things seem.
abstract.cn: 每个判断都始于事物呈现的样子。

examples.en: The house seems very old.
She seems to know the answer.
It seems we have a problem.

branches.en: Someone looks as if doing something.
branches.cn: 某人看起来像是在做某事。

branches.en: A claim is made less direct.

The unseemliness of the joke shocked her.

definition_zh: 部分；片段；细分市场；分割
definition_en: one of the parts into which something divides, a short piece of speech or writing, a group of customers with similar needs, or to divide something into parts
core_image: 一只橘子被一瓣瓣掰开，摆在木桌上
scene: 她把橘子一瓣瓣掰开，分给围坐的孩子。She divided the orange into segments.
sceneCN: 这里 segment 是「部分」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把橘子分成一瓣一瓣的。

senses.title: Natural part
senses.definition: one of the parts into which something naturally divides
senses.definitionCN: 某物自然分成的若干部分之一
senses.example: The orange breaks into easy segments.
senses.exampleCN: 这只橘子很容易分成一瓣瓣。
senses.why: Fruit and animals have natural segments.
senses.whyCN: 水果与动物都有天然的分节部分。

senses.title: Piece of speech
senses.definition: a short piece of speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面材料中的一小段
senses.example: She repeated a segment of the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她重复了采访中的一个片段。
senses.why: A broadcast or text is cut into segments.
senses.whyCN: 广播或文本常被切分成若干片段。

senses.title: Market group
senses.definition: a group of customers with similar needs
senses.definitionCN: 需求相似的顾客群体
senses.example: The ad targets a young segment.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告针对年轻群体。
senses.why: Marketers split buyers into segments.
senses.whyCN: 营销者把买家划分成不同细分群体。

senses.title: Divide
senses.definition: to divide something into parts
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成若干部分
senses.example: The company segmented its market.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司细分了自己的市场。
senses.why: The noun became a verb meaning to split.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示切分的动词。

intro.en: Segment comes from Latin segmentum, a cutting, from secare, to cut.
intro.cn: segment 源自拉丁语 segmentum（切下之物），出自 secare（切）。

items.en: Secare meant to cut.
items.cn: secare 意为切。

items.en: Segmentum named a piece cut off.
items.cn: segmentum 指切下来的一块。

items.en: English used segment for a geometric part.
items.cn: 英语用 segment 指几何上的一段。

items.en: The word spread to speech and biology.
items.cn: 该词扩展到言语与生物学领域。

items.en: Business adopted it for market groups.
items.cn: 商业领域用它指市场细分群体。

note.en: Segment is compared with similar-looking words and with words for parts.
note.cn: 把 segment 与形近词以及表示部分的词作比较。

entries.definition: the act of dividing into parts
one of the parts of something
a part of an economy or area

normalIntro.en: Segment means a piece cut or divided from a whole.
normalIntro.cn: segment 意为从整体中切分出来的一块。

normal.en: An orange is easy to split into segments.
normal.cn: 橘子很容易分成一瓣瓣。

normal.en: A line segment has two endpoints.
normal.cn: 线段有两个端点。

normal.en: A radio show is made of segments.
normal.cn: 广播节目由若干片段组成。

normal.en: Marketers divide buyers into segments.
normal.cn: 营销者把买家分成细分群体。

normal.en: Segment shares the root sect, meaning cut.
normal.cn: segment 与表示「切」的词根 sect 同源。

abstract.en: Every whole can be seen as a set of segments.
abstract.cn: 每个整体都可以看作若干部分。

abstract.en: A segment is meaningful only against its whole.
abstract.cn: 一个片段只有对照整体才有意义。

abstract.en: Choosing your segment changes what you see.
abstract.cn: 选择哪个片段，会改变你看到的东西。

examples.en: The orange breaks into easy segments.
examples.cn: 这只橘子很容易分成一瓣瓣。

examples.en: She repeated a segment of the interview.
examples.cn: 她重复了采访中的一个片段。

examples.en: The ad targets a young segment.
examples.cn: 这则广告针对年轻群体。

dict_mnemonic.text: segment 由拉丁词干 seg（切）加 -ment 构成，本义「切下的一块」，引申为部分、片段与市场细分。

root: 源自拉丁语 segmentum（切下的一块），出自 secare（切），核心义「切分出来的一段」。

core.cn: 从更大整体中分离出来的一块。

branches.en: A natural division of fruit or body.
branches.cn: 水果或身体天然的分节部分。

branches.en: A short piece of talk or text.
branches.cn: 讲话或文本的一小段。

branches.en: A group of similar customers.
branches.cn: 需求相似的一群顾客。

branches.en: The act of splitting into parts.
branches.cn: 把整体切成部分的动作。

branches.en: The noun and verb share one cutting image.
branches.cn: 名词与动词共享同一个「切分」意象。

intro.cn: segment 属于拉丁词干 sect（切）这一词族。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 segmentum 与 secare 是历史词根。

items.meaning: a part cut from a whole
items.example: Each segment of the pipe fits tightly.
items.exampleCN: 每一节管子都接得很紧。

items.example: The worm has a segmental body.

items.exampleCN: 市场细分指导着这项计划。

items.example: The society had a segmentary structure.
items.exampleCN: 这个社会具有分段结构。

items.example: They dissect a fish in class.
items.exampleCN: 他们在课上解剖一条鱼。

items.example: The lines intersect at a point.
Bisect the square with a line.
items.exampleCN: 用一条线把正方形平分。

definition_en: to take hold of something suddenly, to take power by force, to find and take illegal goods, or to take an opportunity quickly
core_image: 球擦着指尖飞过，一只手在半空中猛地收拢
scene: 球飞过来的那一瞬，他猛地伸手把球抓住。He seized the ball with both hands.
sceneCN: 这里 seize 是「抓住」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用双手抓住了球。

senses.title: Take hold suddenly
senses.definition: to take hold of something quickly and firmly
senses.definitionCN: 迅速而牢牢地抓住某物
senses.example: He seized the rope and pulled.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓住绳子用力拉。
senses.why: The basic sense is a sudden grab.
senses.whyCN: 基本义就是突然抓取。

senses.title: Take power
senses.definition: to take control of something by force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力取得对某物的控制
senses.example: The army seized the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 军队夺取了首都。
senses.why: Grabbing extends to political control.
senses.whyCN: 抓取的动作延伸到政治控制。

senses.title: Confiscate
senses.definition: to find and take illegal or forbidden goods
senses.definitionCN: 查获并拿走非法或违禁物品
senses.example: Customs seized the smuggled goods.
senses.exampleCN: 海关查获了走私货物。
senses.why: Officials seize what is not allowed.
senses.whyCN: 官员扣押不允许的物品。

senses.title: Take an opportunity
senses.definition: to take an opportunity quickly before it passes
senses.definitionCN: 趁机会尚未溜走而迅速抓住
senses.example: She seized the chance to study abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她抓住机会出国留学。
senses.why: An opportunity is grabbed like an object.
senses.whyCN: 机会像实物一样被一把抓住。

intro.en: Seize comes from Old French seisir, to take possession, of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: seize 源自古法语 seisir（占有），其根源为日耳曼语。

items.en: Seisir meant to put in possession.
items.cn: seisir 意为使占有。

items.en: Legal French used it for taking property.
items.cn: 法律法语用它表示取得财产。

items.en: English seisen meant to take by force.
items.cn: 英语 seisen 意为以武力夺取。

items.en: The spelling settled as seize.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 seize。

items.en: The word also covers chances and emotions.
items.cn: 该词也用于机会与情绪的「抓住」。

note.en: Seize is compared with similar-sounding words and with verbs of grabbing.
note.cn: 把 seize 与近音词以及表示抓取的动词作比较。

entries.definition: how large or small something is
to take something roughly and quickly
to take a person or place by force

normalIntro.en: Seize means to grab or take control quickly.
normalIntro.cn: seize 意为迅速抓住或取得控制。

normal.en: Seize sounds like sees but means grab.
normal.cn: seize 读音像 sees，意思却是抓。

normal.en: You seize a chance before it disappears.
normal.cn: 机会消失之前要一把抓住。

normal.en: Police seize illegal goods.
normal.cn: 警察查获非法货物。

normal.en: An army can seize a city.
normal.cn: 军队可以夺取一座城市。

normal.en: The noun is seizure, not seizing only.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 seizure。

abstract.en: To seize is to close the distance in an instant.
abstract.cn: 抓住，就是在一瞬间消除距离。

abstract.en: Power taken by force must be held by force.
abstract.cn: 以强力夺来的权力，只能靠强力维持。

abstract.en: Some chances pass in the time it takes to think.
abstract.cn: 有些机会，在思考的工夫里就过去了。

examples.en: He seized the rope and pulled.
Customs seized the smuggled goods.
She seized the chance to study abroad.

dict_mnemonic.text: seize 经古法语 seisir（占有）进入英语，核心是「一把抓过来」，由此引申为夺取、查获与把握机会。

root: 源自古法语 seisir（使占有），根源为日耳曼语，核心义「突然抓住并占为己有」。

sensesIntro.en: Seize means to grab, to take by force, to confiscate, or to take a chance.
sensesIntro.cn: seize 意为抓住、夺取、查获或把握机会。

core.en: To close a hand on something before it escapes.
core.cn: 在某物逃脱之前把手合拢。

branches.en: A hand closes on an object.
branches.cn: 一只手合拢抓住物体。

branches.en: One side takes control of a place.
branches.cn: 一方取得对某地的控制。

branches.en: Officials take forbidden goods.
branches.cn: 官员拿走违禁物品。

branches.en: A person acts before time runs out.
branches.cn: 人在时机消失前行动。

branches.en: Grabbing objects and chances feel the same.
branches.cn: 抓实物与抓机会的感觉是一样的。

intro.en: Seize has a few legal relatives and a common noun in seizure.
intro.cn: seize 有几个法律相关词，名词 seizure 最常用。

latinIntro.en: The word came through French from Germanic, so there are no Latin base forms to add.

items.example: Seize the rope before it slips.
He seizes every chance to practise.
items.exampleCN: 他抓住每个练习的机会。

items.example: The seizing of the port shocked many.
items.exampleCN: 港口被占领让许多人震惊。

items.meaning: a taking by force or a sudden fit
items.example: The seizure of the ship caused a dispute.
The goods are seizable by law.
items.exampleCN: 这些货物依法可以扣押。

items.example: They were disseized of their land.
items.exampleCN: 他们的土地被非法剥夺。

items.example: The court heard a claim of disseisin.
items.exampleCN: 法院审理了一起非法剥夺占有的诉讼。

definition_en: to choose someone or something carefully, or of specially good quality
core_image: 果摊前的木箱里，红透的苹果被一只只手翻拣
scene: 他在果摊前比较了半天，最后挑了最红的那几个。He selected the ripest apples.
sceneCN: 这里 select 是「挑选」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他挑出了最熟的几个苹果。

senses.title: Choose
senses.definition: to choose something from a group
senses.definitionCN: 从一组事物中作出选择
senses.example: She selected a book from the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 她从书架上选了一本书。
senses.why: This is the basic verb sense of choosing.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示「选择」的基本动词义。

senses.title: Pick for a role
senses.definition: to choose someone for a special purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的挑选某人
senses.example: The coach selected three new players.
senses.exampleCN: 教练挑选了三名新队员。
senses.why: Selection often means choosing people for a task.
senses.whyCN: 挑选常指为人选安排某项任务。

senses.title: Of high quality
senses.definition: specially chosen as being the best
senses.definitionCN: 作为最好的而特别挑出的
senses.example: The shop sells select wines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售精选葡萄酒。
senses.why: The adjective marks goods of chosen quality.
senses.whyCN: 形容词表示经过挑选的上等货品。

intro.en: Select comes from Latin seligere, to pick out, from se- apart and legere to choose.
intro.cn: select 源自拉丁语 seligere（挑出），由 se-（分开）与 legere（选择）构成。

items.en: Legere meant to gather or choose.
items.cn: legere 意为采集、选择。

items.en: Seligere meant to pick out from others.
items.cn: seligere 意为从其他事物中挑出。

items.en: Selectus was its past participle.
items.cn: selectus 是它的过去分词。

items.en: English select first described chosen things.
items.cn: 英语 select 最初形容被挑出的东西。

items.en: The verb sense of choosing became common.
items.cn: 表示选择的动词义变得普遍。

note.en: Select is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs of choosing.
note.cn: 把 select 与形近词以及表示选择的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a person or device that chooses

normalIntro.en: Select means to pick out carefully from a group.
normalIntro.cn: select 意为从一组中仔细挑出。

normal.en: The prefix se- means apart.
normal.cn: 前缀 se- 意为「分开」。

normal.en: Legere means to choose, so select is to choose out.
normal.cn: legere 意为选择，所以 select 就是挑出来。

normal.en: A select few are chosen from many.
normal.cn: 少数入选者是从众多人中选出的。

normal.en: Select wines are the best of a cellar.
normal.cn: 精选葡萄酒是酒窖里最好的。

normal.en: Selection is the noun from select.
normal.cn: selection 是 select 的名词形式。

abstract.en: To select is to say no to almost everything.
abstract.cn: 选择，就是对几乎所有选项说不。

abstract.en: What we select reveals what we value.
abstract.cn: 我们挑选什么，就显露我们看重什么。

abstract.en: A choice made carefully can be explained later.
abstract.cn: 慎重作出的选择，日后说得清理由。

examples.en: She selected a book from the shelf.
examples.cn: 她从书架上选了一本书。

examples.en: The coach selected three new players.
examples.cn: 教练挑选了三名新队员。

examples.en: The shop sells select wines.
examples.cn: 这家店出售精选葡萄酒。

core.en: To pick one out from many.
core.cn: 从众多之中挑出一个。

branches.en: One thing is chosen from a group.
branches.cn: 从一组中选出一件。

branches.en: A person is chosen for a task.
branches.cn: 为一项任务选出一个人。

branches.en: Goods are marked as chosen quality.
branches.cn: 货品被标为精选上等。

branches.en: Choosing things and people share one verb.
branches.cn: 选物与选人共用一个动词。

branches.en: Quality is the result of careful choosing.
branches.cn: 上等品质正是精挑细选的结果。

intro.cn: select 属于拉丁词根 legere（选择、采集）这一词族。

items.example: Select the answer that fits best.
The selection process takes a week.

items.exampleCN: 这种药有选择地起作用。

items.meaning: a person or device that selects
items.example: Turn the selector to the left.

definition_zh: 选择；精选品；可选择的范围；选拔
definition_en: the act of choosing, a group of chosen things, the range from which you can choose, or the process of choosing people for a team
core_image: 书店推荐台上，几本新书并排立着，封面朝向读者
scene: 店员把几本新书并排摆在推荐台上。The shop offers a wide selection of novels.
sceneCN: 这里 selection 是「可选择的范围」（第 3 个义项）；句意：这家店提供种类繁多的小说供选择。

senses.title: Act of choosing
senses.definition: the act of choosing something
senses.definitionCN: 挑选某物的行为
senses.example: Her selection of the theme surprised us.
senses.exampleCN: 她选择的主题让我们吃惊。
senses.why: This is the abstract noun for the act of choosing.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示「选择行为」的抽象名词。

senses.title: Chosen things
senses.definition: a group of things chosen from a larger set
senses.definitionCN: 从更大多集中挑选出来的一组事物
senses.example: The album collects a selection of his songs.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑收录了他的精选歌曲。
senses.why: The result of choosing is a selection.
senses.whyCN: 挑选的结果本身就是一批精选品。

senses.title: Range to choose from
senses.definition: the range of things available to choose from
senses.definitionCN: 可供挑选的事物范围
senses.example: The menu offers a wide selection.
senses.exampleCN: 菜单上的选择很丰富。
senses.why: A shop's selection is everything it offers.
senses.whyCN: 商店的 selection 就是它提供的全部货品。

senses.title: Choosing players
senses.definition: the process of choosing people for a team or job
senses.definitionCN: 为队伍或职位挑选人员的过程
senses.example: His selection for the team was deserved.
senses.exampleCN: 他入选队伍是应得的。
senses.why: Sports and jobs use selection for people.
senses.whyCN: 体育与招聘用 selection 指人员选拔。

items.en: English selection named the act and the result.

items.en: Shops used it for the range on offer.

items.en: Science adopted natural selection.

note.en: Selection is compared with similar-looking words and with words for choice and range.

normal.en: Selection is the noun from select.

normal.en: A wide selection means many things to choose from.

abstract.en: The range you are offered shapes the choice you make.

definition_en: the person you are, your own nature or character, or your own interests

senses.title: The person you are

definition_en: caring only about your own needs and not about other people
core_image: 最后一块蛋糕被一只手端走，盘子里只剩奶油痕
scene: 最后一块蛋糕被他端走，谁也没分到。It was selfish of him to take the last piece.
sceneCN: 这里 selfish 是「自私的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他拿走最后一块，真是太自私了。

senses.title: Putting oneself first
senses.definition: caring only about your own needs
senses.definitionCN: 只关心自己的需要
senses.example: It was selfish of him to take the last piece.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿走最后一块，真是太自私了。
senses.why: This is the core sense of self-interest.
senses.whyCN: 这是「只顾自己」的核心义。

senses.title: Not generous
senses.definition: unwilling to share with other people
senses.definitionCN: 不愿与他人分享
senses.example: She kept the whole secret in a selfish way.
senses.exampleCN: 她自私地把整个秘密藏在心里。
senses.why: Failure to share is a common form of selfishness.
senses.whyCN: 不愿分享是自私的常见表现。

senses.title: Motivated by self-interest
senses.definition: done mainly for your own advantage
senses.definitionCN: 主要为了自己的好处而做
senses.example: He helped only for selfish reasons.
senses.exampleCN: 他帮忙只是出于私利。
senses.why: An act can be selfish without being cruel.
senses.whyCN: 一个行为可以自私，却未必残忍。

items.en: Self named the same person.
